questions.q: Which of the following is the most stable complex?
questions.explanation: Oxalate is a bidentate chelating ligand, and chelation (forming multiple stable rings) gives [Fe(C$_2$O$_4$)$_3$]$^{3-}$ exceptional stability compared to the other listed complexes.

questions.q: How many ions per molecule are produced from the complex [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]Cl$_3$ in solution?
questions.note: The standard answer is (B) 4 ions: [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]Cl$_3$ dissociates into one [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{3+}$ complex ion and 3 Cl$^-$ ions, totalling 4 ions per formula unit, not 3.
questions.explanation: [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]Cl$_3$ ionises as [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{3+}$ + 3Cl$^-$, which gives 4 ions in total (option B); the KEA key for this version marks option C (3 ions) — the key's answer is retained here (as per KEA key).

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The M - C $\sigma$ bond is formed by the donation of lone pair of electrons on the carbonyl carbon into a vacant d-orbital of the metal
Statement II: The M - C $\pi$ bond is formed by the donation of a pair of electrons from a filled d-orbital of metal into the vacant antibonding $\pi^*$ orbital of carbon monoxide.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: This is the standard synergic bonding description in metal carbonyls: a $\sigma$-donation from carbon to metal plus $\pi$-back-donation from metal to CO's $\pi^*$ orbital — both statements are correct.

questions.q:
Match List - I with List - II
List - I (Complex): (a) [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{3+}$ (b) [NiCl$_4$]$^{2-}$ (c) [Ni(CN)$_4$]$^{2-}$ (d) [Fe(CO)$_5$]
List - II (Geometry): (i) Trigonal bipyramidal (ii) Octahedral (iii) Tetrahedral (iv) Square planar
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: a - ii, b - iii, c - iv, d - i
a - ii, b - i, c - iii, d - iv
a - iii, b - ii, c - iv, d - i
a - i, b - iii, c - iv, d - ii
questions.explanation: [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{3+}$ is octahedral, [NiCl$_4$]$^{2-}$ is tetrahedral, [Ni(CN)$_4$]$^{2-}$ is square planar, and [Fe(CO)$_5$] is trigonal bipyramidal.

questions.q: A ligand which has two different donor atoms and either of the two ligates with the central metal atom/ion in the complex is called ________
questions.explanation: An ambidentate ligand (e.g. NO$_2^-$, SCN$^-$) has two different donor atoms but coordinates through only one of them at a time.

questions.q: Which of the following statements are true about [NiCl$_4$]$^{2-}$? (a) The complex has tetrahedral geometry. (b) Co-ordination number of Ni is 2 and oxidation state is +4. (c) The complex is sp$^3$ hybridised (d) It is a high spin complex. (e) The complex is paramagnetic.
questions.explanation: [NiCl$_4$]$^{2-}$ has Ni$^{2+}$ (d$^8$) with coordination number 4 and oxidation state +2, so (b) is false; the complex is tetrahedral, sp$^3$ hybridised, high spin and paramagnetic, giving statements a, c, d and e.

questions.q: Which formula and its name combination is incorrect?
questions.explanation: CO$_3^{2-}$ acting as a ligand is named 'carbonato', not 'carbonyl' (which refers to CO), so the name in option 4 (originally keyed) is incorrect; however, option 1's name 'chloridonitrito' also mixes up the naming convention (should be nitrito-O or nitrito-N specified consistently), so KEA's revised key accepted both option 1 and option 4.

questions.q: In the complex ion [Fe(C$_2$O$_4$)$_3$]$^{3-}$, the co-ordination number of Fe is
questions.explanation: Oxalate (C$_2$O$_4^{2-}$) is a bidentate ligand, so three oxalate ions occupy 3×2=6 coordination positions around Fe.

questions.q: On treating 100 mL of 0.1 M aqueous solution of the complex CrCl$_3$.6H$_2$O with excess of AgNO$_3$, 2.86 g of AgCl was obtained. The complex is
questions.explanation: 0.01 mol of complex gives 0.02 mol AgCl (2.86 g / 143.5 g mol$^{-1}$), so 2 Cl$^-$ ions are ionisable, giving the formula [Cr(H$_2$O)$_5$Cl]Cl$_2$.H$_2$O.

questions.q: The complex compounds [Co(NH$_3$)$_5$SO$_4$]Br and [Co(NH$_3$)$_5$Br]SO$_4$ are
questions.explanation: They differ in which ion (Br$^-$ or SO$_4^{2-}$) lies inside versus outside the coordination sphere, which is the defining feature of ionisation isomerism.

questions.q: When of the following statements are true about [CoF$_6$]$^{3-}$ ion? I) The complex has octahedral geometry. II) Coordination number of Co is 3 and oxidation state is +6. III) The complex is sp$^3$d$^2$ hybridised. IV) It is a high spin complex.
questions.explanation: [CoF$_6$]$^{3-}$ is octahedral (I) with Co in the +3 state and coordination number 6 (so II is false); the weak-field F$^-$ ligand gives an sp$^3$d$^2$ hybridised, high-spin complex (III and IV true).

questions.q: If a didentate ligand ethane-1,2-diamine is progressively added in the molar ratio en : Ni :: 1:1, 2:1, 3:1 to [Ni(H$_2$O)$_6$]$^{2+}$ aq solution, following co-ordination entities are formed. I. [Ni(H$_2$O)$_4$en]$^{2+}_{(aq)}$ - pale blue. II. [Ni(H$_2$O)$_2$(en)$_2$]$^{2+}_{(aq)}$ - blue/purple. III. [Ni(en)$_3$]$^{2+}_{(aq)}$ - violet. The wavelength in nm of light absorbed in case of I and III are respectively
questions.explanation: en is a stronger-field ligand than H$_2$O, so each successive substitution increases the crystal field splitting $\Delta_o$; the least-substituted complex I therefore absorbs lower-energy, longer-wavelength light (about 600 nm) while the fully en-substituted complex III absorbs higher-energy, shorter-wavelength light (about 535 nm).

questions.q: Which formula and name combination is INCORRECT ?
questions.explanation: In [CoCl$_2$(en)$_2$]Cl, the two Cl$^-$ ligands inside the coordination sphere plus one Cl$^-$ counter-ion require cobalt to be +3, so the correct name is cobalt(III), not cobalt(II) as given; the other three formula-name pairs are correctly assigned.

questions.q: Which of the following system in an octahedral complex has maximum unpaired electrons ?
questions.explanation: d$^9$(high spin) has 1 unpaired electron, d$^6$(low spin) has 0, d$^4$(low spin) has 2, while d$^7$(high spin) has 3 unpaired electrons (t$_{2g}^5$e$_g^2$), the maximum among these.

questions.q: The complex hexaamine platinum (IV) chloride will give _____ number of ions on ionization.
questions.explanation: [Pt(NH$_3$)$_6$]Cl$_4$ ionizes into one complex cation [Pt(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{4+}$ and four Cl$^-$ ions, giving 5 ions in total.

questions.q: The correct IUPAC name of cis-platin is
questions.explanation: Cis-platin is [PtCl$_2$(NH$_3$)$_2$] with platinum in the +2 oxidation state, named diamminedichloridoplatinum(II).

questions.q: Crystal Field Splitting Energy (CFSE) for [CoCl$_6$]$^{4-}$ is 18000 cm$^{-1}$. The Crystal Field Splitting Energy (CFSE) for [CoCl$_4$]$^{2-}$ will be
For the crystal field splitting in octahedral complexes,
options: the energy of the e$_g$ orbitals will decrease by (3/5)Δ$_0$ and that of the t$_{2g}$ will increase by (2/5)Δ$_0$
the energy of the e$_g$ orbitals will increase by (3/5)Δ$_0$ and that of the t$_{2g}$ will decrease by (2/5)Δ$_0$
the energy of the e$_g$ orbitals will increase by (3/5)Δ$_0$ and that of the t$_{2g}$ will increase by (2/5)Δ$_0$
the energy of the e$_g$ orbitals will decrease by (3/5)Δ$_0$ and that of the t$_{2g}$ will decrease by (2/5)Δ$_0$
questions.explanation: In octahedral crystal field splitting, e$_g$ orbitals are raised by (3/5)Δ$_0$ while t$_{2g}$ orbitals are lowered by (2/5)Δ$_0$ relative to the barycentre.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of [Co(NH$_3$)$_5$(CO$_3$)] Cl is
questions.explanation: Ligands are named alphabetically (ammine before carbonato) as prefixes to the metal name, giving Pentaamminecarbonatocobalt(III) Chloride; since the complex ion is a cation, no '-ate' suffix is used.

questions.q: Homoleptic complexes among the following are: (A) K$_3$[Al(C$_2$O$_4$)$_3$], (B) [CoCl(en)$_2$]$^+$ (C) K$_2$[Zn(OH)$_4$]
questions.explanation: Homoleptic complexes have only one kind of ligand: K$_3$[Al(C$_2$O$_4$)$_3$] (only oxalate) and K$_2$[Zn(OH)$_4$] (only hydroxide) are homoleptic; [CoCl(en)$_2$]$^+$ has two different ligands (heteroleptic).

questions.q: The correct order for wavelengths of light absorbed in the complex ions [CoCl(NH$_3$)$_5$]$^{2+}$, [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{3+}$ and [Co(CN)$_6$]$^{3-}$ is
questions.explanation: By the spectrochemical series Cl$^-$ < NH$_3$ < CN$^-$, crystal field splitting Δ$_0$ increases in that order, and wavelength absorbed is inversely related to Δ$_0$, giving [CoCl(NH$_3$)$_5$]$^{2+}$ > [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{3+}$ > [Co(CN)$_6$]$^{3-}$.

questions.q: The co-ordination number of Fe and Co in the complex ions, [Fe(C$_2$O$_4$)$_3$]$^{3-}$ and [Co(SCN)$_4$]$^{2-}$ are respectively:
questions.explanation: Oxalate is a bidentate ligand, so 3 oxalates give coordination number 6 for Fe; SCN$^-$ is monodentate, so 4 SCN$^-$ give coordination number 4 for Co.

questions.q: Number of stereoisomers exhibited by [Co(en)$_2$Cl$_2$]$^+$ is
questions.explanation: This [M(AA)$_2$B$_2$] complex shows a chiral cis form (a pair of enantiomers) and an achiral trans form, giving 3 stereoisomers in total.

questions.q: Give the IUPAC name of [Pt(NH$_3$)$_4$][PtCl$_4$] is
options: tetra ammine platinum(II) tetra chlorido platinate(II)
tetra ammine platinum(o) tetra chlorido platinum(IV)
tetra ammine platinate(II) tetra chlorido platinum(II)
tetra ammine platinate(o) tetra chlorido platinum(IV)
questions.explanation: The cation [Pt(NH$_3$)$_4$]$^{2+}$ is tetraamminplatinum(II) and the anion [PtCl$_4$]$^{2-}$ is tetrachloridoplatinate(II).

questions.q: Which among the following is the strongest ligand?
questions.explanation: In the spectrochemical series, CO produces the largest crystal field splitting and is considered the strongest ligand among these choices.

questions.q: Addition of excess of AgNO$_3$ to an aqueous solution of 1 mole of PdCl$_2$.4NH$_3$ gives 2 moles of AgCl. The conductivity of this solution corresponds to
questions.explanation: Since 2 mol of ionisable Cl- are precipitated per mole of complex, the compound must be [Pd(NH3)4]Cl2, which ionises as 1 cation : 2 anions, i.e. a 1:2 electrolyte.

questions.q: The formula of penta aquanitrato chromium (III) nitrate is
questions.explanation: Penta aqua nitrato chromium(III) has the coordination sphere [Cr(H2O)5(NO3)]2+, balanced by two nitrate counter ions: [Cr(H2O)5NO3](NO3)2.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of [Co(NH$_3$)$_4$Cl(NO$_2$)]Cl is
questions.explanation: Ligands are named alphabetically (ammine, chlorido, nitrito-N for N-bonded NO$_2^-$); charge balance with one ionisable Cl$^-$ gives Co oxidation state +3, so the name is tetraamminechloridonitrito-N-cobalt(III) chloride.

questions.q: [Fe(NO$_2$)$_3$Cl$_3$] and [Fe(O-NO)$_3$Cl$_3$] shows
questions.explanation: The ambidentate NO$_2^-$ ligand can bind through N (nitro) or through O (nitrito), giving linkage isomers.

questions.q: Square planar complex of the type MAXBL (where A, B, X and L are unidentate ligands) shows following set of isomers
questions.explanation: A square planar M(A)(X)(B)(L) complex with four different unidentate ligands exists as three geometrical isomers; per the KEA key these are described as two cis and one trans arrangement.

questions.q: According to crystal field theory, the M – L bond in a complex is
questions.explanation: Crystal field theory treats the metal–ligand interaction as a purely electrostatic (ionic) attraction between the metal cation and the ligands.

questions.q: The co-ordination number and the oxidation state of the element 'M' in the complex [M(en)$_2$(C$_2$O$_4$)]NO$_2$ {where (en) is ethan-1,2-diamine} are respectively
questions.explanation: Two bidentate en ligands (4 donor sites) plus one bidentate oxalate (2 donor sites) give coordination number 6; with NO$_2^-$ as the counter ion the complex ion is +1, so M + 0 − 2 = +1, giving M = +3.

questions.q: The number of isomers possible for the octahedral complex [CoCl$_2$(en)(NH$_3$)$_2$]$^+$ is,
questions.note: The standard count is three isomers: a trans (achiral) form plus a cis form that is chiral (a pair of optical enantiomers) = 1 + 2 = 3. The KEA key credits option (4), four isomers.
questions.explanation: The complex [CoCl$_2$(en)(NH$_3$)$_2$]$^+$ shows cis/trans geometrical isomerism, with the cis form additionally being chiral (optically active); KEA's key credits four isomers as the answer.

questions.q: CO is a stronger ligand than Cl$^-$, because
questions.explanation: CO is a strong-field ligand because its empty $\pi^*$ orbitals accept back-donated electron density from the metal ($\pi$-acceptor behaviour).

questions.q: Which of the following sequence is correct regarding field strength of ligands as per spectrochemical series ?
questions.explanation: In the spectrochemical series, field strength increases as SCN$^-$ < F$^-$ < ... < CN$^-$ < CO, with CO and CN$^-$ being the strongest field ligands.

questions.q: As per IUPAC norms, the name of the complex [Co(en)$_2$(ONO)Cl]Cl is
options: Chlorido di(ethylene diamine) nitro cobalt (III) chloride.
questions.explanation: Ligands are cited alphabetically as chlorido, bis(ethane-1,2-diamine), nitrito-O-, giving option (1); a grace mark was awarded for this question, likely due to the imprecise "nitro-o" wording in the options.

questions.q: Which of the following will be able to show geometrical isomerism?
questions.explanation: Tetrahedral complexes are too symmetric to show geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism, and MA$_3$B square planar has only one possible arrangement; a square planar MABCD complex with four different ligands can have distinct cis/trans arrangements and shows geometrical isomerism.

questions.q: How many ions per molecule are produced in the solution when Mohr salt is dissolved in excess of water?
questions.explanation: Mohr's salt, FeSO$_4$.(NH$_4$)$_2$SO$_4$.6H$_2$O, is a double salt that dissociates completely into Fe$^{2+}$ (1) + 2NH$_4^+$ (2) + 2SO$_4^{2-}$ (2) = 5 ions.

questions.q: The complex ion having minimum magnitude of $\Delta_0$(CFSE) is
questions.explanation: In the spectrochemical series Cl$^-$ is a weaker-field ligand than H$_2$O, NH$_3$ and CN$^-$, so [Co(Cl)$_6$]$^{3-}$ causes the smallest crystal field splitting $\Delta_0$.

questions.q: A correct statement is
questions.explanation: [MnBr$_4$]$^{2-}$ (Mn$^{2+}$, d$^5$, weak field Br$^-$) is tetrahedral, and [Co(NH$_3$)$_6$]$^{2+}$ (Co$^{2+}$, d$^7$, weak field NH$_3$ for Co$^{2+}$) is high spin and paramagnetic; both (3) and (4) are correct, so both C and D are accepted.

questions.q: In which one of the pairs of ion given, there is an ion that forms a co-ordination compound with both aqueous sodium hydroxide and ammonia and an other ion that forms a co-ordination compound only with aqueous sodium hydroxide?
questions.explanation: Zn$^{2+}$ (amphoteric) forms a co-ordination compound with both excess aqueous NaOH ([Zn(OH)$_4$]$^{2-}$, zincate) and with ammonia ([Zn(NH$_3$)$_4$]$^{2+}$), while Al$^{3+}$ forms a complex only with excess NaOH ([Al(OH)$_4$]$^-$, aluminate) and not with NH$_3$ (Al(OH)$_3$ does not dissolve in ammonia); so the pair Zn$^{2+}$, Al$^{3+}$ fits.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of the complex ion formed when gold dissolves in aquaregia is
questions.explanation: Gold dissolves in aqua regia to form the complex ion [AuCl$_4$]$^-$, in which gold is in the +3 oxidation state, named tetrachloridoaurate(III).

questions.q: d$^2$sp$^3$ hybridisation of the atomic orbitals gives
questions.explanation: d$^2$sp$^3$ (or sp$^3$d$^2$) hybridisation involves six orbitals directed octahedrally, giving an octahedral structure.

questions.q: A group of atoms can function as a ligand only when
options: it has an unshared electron pair.
it is a negatively charged ion.
it is a positively charged ion.
questions.explanation: A ligand donates a lone pair of electrons to the central metal atom/ion to form a coordinate bond.

questions.q: The atomic number of cobalt is 27. The EAN of cobalt in Na$_3$[Co(NO$_2$)$_4$Cl$_2$] is
questions.explanation: Co is in +3 state (losing 3 electrons: Z-3=24), and EAN = 24 + 2×(coordination number 6) = 24+12=36.

questions.q: The 'spin only' magnetic moment of Ni$^{2+}$ in aqueous solution would be [At. No. of Ni = 28]
questions.explanation: Ni$^{2+}$ (d$^8$) has 2 unpaired electrons; $\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{2\times4}=\sqrt8$ BM.

questions.q: A ligand is
options: either a Lewis acid or a Lewis base
questions.explanation: A ligand donates an electron pair to the central metal atom/ion, so it acts as a Lewis base.

questions.q: Which of the following is a negatively charged bidentate ligand?
questions.explanation: Dimethylglyoximato ion is a bidentate ligand binding through two deprotonated oxygen atoms and carries a negative charge; cyano is monodentate, ethylenediamine is neutral bidentate, acetato is monodentate/negatively charged.

questions.q: The secondary valency of platinum in tetra ammine dichloroplatinum (IV) chloride is
questions.explanation: In [Pt(NH$_3$)$_4$Cl$_2$]Cl$_2$, platinum is coordinated to 4 NH$_3$ and 2 Cl ligands, giving a secondary valency (coordination number) of 6.

questions.q: Which one of the following has a magnetic moment of 1.75 BM?
questions.explanation: Ti$^{3+}$ (d$^1$) has one unpaired electron; $\mu=\sqrt{1\times3}=\sqrt3\approx1.73\approx1.75$ BM.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of the complex $[Co(NH_3)_4Cl_2]Cl$ is ..............
questions.explanation: Ligands are named alphabetically (ammine before chloro); the counter ion $Cl^-$ balances a +1 complex ion charge, so cobalt is in the +3 state, giving tetraamminedichlorocobalt(III) chloride.

questions.q: Excess of silver nitrate solution is added to 100 ml of 0.01 M Pentaaqua chloro chromium (III) chloride solution. The mass of silver chloride obtained in grams is .............. [Atomic mass of silver is 108].
questions.explanation: $[Cr(H_2O)_5Cl]Cl_2$ has 2 ionizable $Cl^-$ per formula unit; moles complex = 0.1×0.01=$10^{-3}$, so moles ionizable $Cl^-$=$2\times10^{-3}$; mass $AgCl$=$2\times10^{-3}\times143.5=287\times10^{-3}$ g.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of $K_2[Ni(CN)_4]$ is ...............
questions.explanation: The complex ion is $[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}$ with Ni in +2 state; cyano ligands (CN$^-$) named 'cyano', giving potassium tetracyanonickelate(II).

questions.q: Which one of the following is wrongly matched?
questions.explanation: CN$^-$ is a strong field ligand, so $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$ is low spin with $d^2sp^3$ hybridization, not $sp^3d^2$ (which is used for weak-field, high-spin octahedral complexes).

questions.q: The IUPAC name of [Co(NH$_3$)$_5$ONO]$^{2+}$ ion is
questions.explanation: ONO$^-$ bonded through O is nitrito-O; overall charge +2 with 5 neutral NH$_3$ and -1 nitrito gives Co oxidation state +3, so it is pentaamminenitrito-O-cobalt(III) ion.

questions.q: The oxidation state of Fe in the brown ring complex : [Fe(H$_2$O)$_5$NO]SO$_4$ is
questions.explanation: Treating NO as neutral (or as NO$^+$) in this complex is ambiguous by convention, so KEA accepted both +2 (NO neutral) and +1 (NO$^+$) as correct.
